bug_semantics: Before 0.14.0, c3p0 shipped serializable/indirectly serializable JDBC DataSource and ConnectionPoolDataSource beans with public no-argument getConnection() and getPooledConnection() methods but no explicit BeanInfo excluding those method names. java.beans.Introspector therefore exposed connection and pooledConnection as readable bean properties. A deserialization carrier such as a collection sorted by an Apache commons-beanutils property Comparator could invoke one of those apparent property getters while deserializing an attacker-crafted c3p0 datasource; the getter then entered a JDBC driver using attacker-controlled datasource configuration (the earliest visible DriverManagerDataSource implementation directly calls DriverManager.getConnection(jdbcUrl, properties)). Exploitation additionally requires the relevant c3p0 datasource, a susceptible JDBC driver, and an automatic bean-property-reading carrier on the classpath.
flaw_origin: The true line-authoring origin is outside the available public commit history. The earliest observable vulnerable artifact is reconstructed SourceForge snapshot commit 66e3716e788e0ac8f9c2e8e93711cfee301bede8, tagged c3p0-0.8.4-test1. It bulk-imports c3p0-0.8.4-test1.src.zip and already contains DriverManagerDataSource.java with public getConnection() at lines 61-62 plus BeangenDataSourceGenerator.java line 66 adding IndirectingSerializableExtension. Its immediate parent 0457a1a6340cff65ee20927c36646bf55e95ba83 is an intentionally empty reconstruction root. Because 66e3716e788e0ac8f9c2e8e93711cfee301bede8 is a release-archive snapshot rather than the atomic commit that wrote the vulnerable design, it is a history boundary, not a true BIC.
ai_marker: Unavailable for the true BIC because that commit is not present. For boundary evidence only, `git cat-file -p 66e3716e788e0ac8f9c2e8e93711cfee301bede8` shows author and committer Steve Waldman <swaldman@mchange.com> and message `source imported from SourceForge (c3p0-0.8.4-test1.src.zip)`, with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI marker. That archive-import commit object is not substituted for the missing true BIC and therefore cannot close the AI judgment.
evidence: Advisory GHSA-w6w4-rjh9-9r58 / CVE-2026-55223 states affected Maven versions are < 0.14.0, first patched 0.14.0, and explains that 0.14.0 adds explicit BeanInfo classes excluding connection and pooledConnection. Reproduce the origin boundary in the validated clone with: (1) `git log --first-parent --reverse b3def24567324f3cac4d46ad0121c2768179b1a7`, which begins at empty reconstruction commit 0457a1a6340cff65ee20927c36646bf55e95ba83 and then snapshot 66e3716e788e0ac8f9c2e8e93711cfee301bede8 (`source imported from SourceForge (c3p0-0.8.4-test1.src.zip)`); (2) `git tag --points-at 66e3716e788e0ac8f9c2e8e93711cfee301bede8`, which prints c3p0-0.8.4-test1; (3) `git show 66e3716e788e0ac8f9c2e8e93711cfee301bede8:src/classes/com/mchange/v2/c3p0/DriverManagerDataSource.java`, lines 38 and 61-62, showing the DataSource class and the no-arg getter calling DriverManager.getConnection(jdbcUrl, properties); (4) `git show 66e3716e788e0ac8f9c2e8e93711cfee301bede8:src/classes/com/mchange/v2/c3p0/codegen/BeangenDataSourceGenerator.java`, line 66, showing IndirectingSerializableExtension; (5) `git log -L 61,62:src/classes/com/mchange/v2/c3p0/DriverManagerDataSource.java 66e3716e788e0ac8f9c2e8e93711cfee301bede8` and `git log --all --reverse -S'public Connection getConnection()' -- src/classes/com/mchange/v2/c3p0/DriverManagerDataSource.java`, both reaching the same snapshot; and (6) `git cat-file -p 0457a1a6340cff65ee20927c36646bf55e95ba83` plus `git ls-tree -r --name-only 0457a1a6340cff65ee20927c36646bf55e95ba83`, which show the empty tree and directly verify that the observable snapshot parent lacks the vulnerable source. Reproduce the fix with `git show --format=fuller 7b022c4b6694dabc6204254dc917af9c38f2cb27`: it adds beanInfo/src/com/mchange/v2/c3p0/beaninfo/C3P0BeanInfoGen.java and build.mill integration, with excludedPropertyNames containing connection and pooledConnection and excludedPropertyTypes containing java.sql.Connection and javax.sql.PooledConnection. `git grep -n -E 'public (Connection getConnection|PooledConnection getPooledConnection)\(' e604f8d7599e185803a7fa6584f7076331cbc847 -- src/com/mchange/v2/c3p0` shows the getters in the fix parent, while `git ls-tree -r --name-only e604f8d7599e185803a7fa6584f7076331cbc847 beanInfo` is empty. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 7b022c4b6694dabc6204254dc917af9c38f2cb27 v0.13.0` exits 1; the same command against v0.14.0 exits 0. `git rev-parse 'v0.13.0^{}' 'v0.14.0^{}'` resolves to a8f08227431ebc00bb75486011675b103cff1643 and 931fd53b695720adc4ac087e021b6de7daf0dd1b respectively. RELEASE_NOTES-c3p0-0.14.0 lines 35-41 independently describe the generated BeanInfo exclusion and the malicious-JDBC-URL attack vector.
reasoning: The vulnerability lifecycle and closing patch are verifiable: an affected c3p0 datasource is interpreted as a bean with a dangerous readable connection property, and 7b022c4b6694dabc6204254dc917af9c38f2cb27 directly prevents that introspection before the v0.14.0 release. The earliest preserved vulnerable source is already present in a reconstructed 2003 release zip snapshot whose parent is deliberately empty. That proves an observable lower bound and parent absence for the snapshot, but not the smallest atomic commit that authored the vulnerable getter/serializability combination. Treating the snapshot import as the BIC would violate the protocol's requirement to reject aggregate imports. Since the missing original BIC also means its commit-object AI signal cannot be inspected, neither NOT_AI nor an AI verdict is supportable under the BIC-only evidence rule; the genuine public-history boundary requires BLOCKED.
remaining_gap: Original pre-c3p0-0.8.4-test1 development history (or another authoritative atomic changeset) that identifies the commit which first combined a serializable c3p0 DataSource/ConnectionPoolDataSource with the introspectable no-argument connection getter, its immediate parent, and that true BIC's commit-object author/committer/trailers. The available Git history begins with a later reconstructed SourceForge release-archive import, so this fact cannot be recovered from the validated clone.
